title: RFC-2026-018 and its correction, RFC-2026-019 — how the service path connects

role_assignments._run_id_disambiguation: /claude/r0_steward (Anthropic) is THIS package's Integration Owner and must record its own capability declaration before this package leaves backlog. /root/r0_steward (OpenAI Codex) is a DIFFERENT run: it is the Integration Owner of WP-0A-A0-001 and WP-0A-CON-001 and is named in open_blockers solely because it must countersign the amendments made to those two packages and record the WP-0A-CON-001 npm run check addendum. Neither run substitutes for the other. Independent testing flagged the near-identical names as ambiguous; both are intended.

independence.cross_vendor_exception: prefer_cross_vendor_review is NOT satisfied: every assigned run is Anthropic claude-opus-5. The Decision Register (§ cross-vendor review) permits this only as an explicit exception - 'if there is no cross-vendor capacity, use an independent agent per run and record the exception'. Each of the five roles is a separate agent run with its own capability declaration and no run reviewed, tested, or integrated its own work. The Integration Owner must carry this exception forward; it is not waived and it is not equivalent to cross-vendor review.

required_human_authorities: Product Owner disposition of RFC-2026-017, which closes the half of DATA-DEC-03 RFC-2026-016 left open.
A1 to countersign the role topology before the roles are created, since DATA-DEC-03 is owned A0+A1 and this is a security surface.
purpose:
RFC-2026-017 created the service roles and left the connection method open, saying so in 001_service_roles.sql. Measured on 2026-09-06, nothing can become app_worker, app_command or app_maintenance except postgres, which bypasses RLS -- so the RFC's present tense describes no reachable path. This package proposes the connection method as its own decision rather than letting it be settled by whoever writes the first line of application code.

RFC-2026-018 was approved and then found to rest on a misreading of RFC-2026-017 §3: it treated app_command as a role the request path assumes, when §3 defines it as the OWNER of the SECURITY DEFINER command functions. RFC-2026-019 supersedes it. The package keeps both, because a package that quietly replaces its own wrong answer teaches nobody why it was wrong.

include: RFC-2026-017 recording the service-path decision and the role topology it implies
The measurement behind it, taken from the provisioned instance rather than vendor documentation
The costs of the decision, recorded so they are not discovered later as surprises
exclude: Creating the roles. That is a migration, and it belongs to the batch A0 owns, not to a decision record.
Writing any tenant table or policy. Batch 010 is A1 Identity's.
Claiming the isolation is proven. No tenant table exists, so no cross-tenant assertion has run.
Disposing this RFC. That is the Product Owner's act on a disposition branch.

amends_without_owning.rationale: THIS INCREMENT AMENDS NOTHING OUTSIDE THIS PACKAGE. It removes three spent blockers and rewrites one whose conclusion went false, touching only the manifest and the handoff this package owns. The list is emptied rather than left carrying the earlier increment's paths (scripts/verify-test-coverage-floor.mjs, test-kits/branch-identity.test.mjs, test-kits/integrity-manifest.json, test-kits/repository-json.test.mjs), because verify-branch-scope reads the declaration in both directions and a path declared here that this branch does not touch is a standing permission over another package's file granted for work that never happened. Those paths remain in git history.

acceptance_criteria: The RFC states the measurement it rests on, names the instance and the date, and cites no vendor documentation in place of a reading.
It records that authenticator holds no membership in any service role, which is the fact that makes RFC-2026-017 §3's present tense false today.
Every candidate is recorded with what it makes true AND what it costs, including the one that is refused, so a reader can see the option was considered rather than unavailable.
The security question option A raises is answered directly rather than deferred: the capability is already held through service_role, and the option narrows it rather than widening it.
The RFC names what must be true before it can close, in artefacts a build can check, and states that until then RFC-2026-017 §3 stays wrong.
It names what it does NOT decide, including the background worker path and JWT custody.
It changes no migration, no lint and no role. A Proposed decision that has already changed the tree is not a proposal.
RFC-2026-019 states what RFC-2026-018 got wrong in its own words, including which comparison RFC-2026-018 made and which one decides the question.
It names the root error in a form that generalises: a missing COMPONENT was read as a missing GRANT.
Every clause of its decision is assertable against the database as it stands, and it says which rules carry them — including the negative, that authenticator holds no membership in any service role.
It records that the error was not caught by the review, nor by the conflict order, but by reading the two decisions together.
It changes no role, no grant and no migration, exactly as RFC-2026-018 did not.
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert through a reviewed revert PR. Reverting removes a proposal and changes no role, no grant and no lint, because the proposal deliberately changed none.
open_blockers: A1 has not seen this RFC. Its countersignature identified the gap -- the topology is built and not connected -- but identifying a gap is not agreeing with a proposal for filling it.

THE DECISION IS NOW IMPLEMENTED AS FAR AS IT CAN BE, AND THIS BLOCKER USED TO SAY NOTHING IN THE TREE IMPLEMENTED IT. All three rules RFC-2026-019 §5 names are written: `authenticator` holds no membership in the three service roles (scripts/db/run.mjs:307 and the SERVICE_ROLES_NOT_FOR_THE_REQUEST_PATH check beside it), no table in `app` is owned by app_command (scripts/db/run.mjs:632), and every SECURITY DEFINER function carries an empty search_path with its OWNER recorded (scripts/db/run.mjs:1003, against catalog-snapshot.json's security_definer_functions). WHAT IS STILL OWED IS THE FOURTH RULE §5 NAMES AND DOES NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE: when the first command function exists it must be owned by app_command, and an isolation case must call it as `authenticated` and be refused where the policies say it should be. No command function exists, so that case cannot be written, and RFC-2026-021 §10 records that absence rather than this manifest inferring it.
